body:
[A10] Lane C5a of the PP program (milan-fpga #415 comment 5883685470, wave 2: AECP deadlines and the scoreboard). Executor [A462], on branch `c5a-aecp-deadlines` from `main` `0451d83d`. Reviewers [R418] (internal) and [R419] (external). The lane covers #57, #81 and #84. Parent evidence owner: milan-fpga #76.

**Design first.** Before any code, write the design in HANDOFF.md:
- where the transaction deadline is read;
- how the deadline-kill face reaches the scoreboard inside `protocol_processor_top` (today it is tied off);
- how the six missing F03.7 hazard classes reach it.

Cite 08 §4, F03.7 and the Milan and IEEE 1722.1 AECP response-time clauses. Post the design summary as a STOP for a manager ruling if it needs a top-level port, a parameter or a parent-visible change. Otherwise proceed.

**Items, in order:**
1. **#81 (GAP-07):** the 08 §4 budgets realized: the transaction deadline is read, and the scoreboard kill face is connected.
2. **#57 (REQ-MVU-005):** T-AECP-RESP. The deadline-kill seam is exercised, and a suite measures MVU response latency against its budget.
3. **#84 (GAP-10):** all nine F03.7 classes reach the scoreboard, each with a failing arm.

Each item has mutants on the named check, and the resource cost is reported (LUT and FF, out of context).

4. **The parent-visible list.**

**Gates:** as for every PP lane, with the parent consumer set at milan-fpga dev `ccdd07b5` and the combined parent adaptation applied.

Do not edit or delete any existing comment.

[A10] Round 2 for PR #140 (lane C5a, AECP deadlines). Executor [A466], on branch `c5a-aecp-deadlines` at `f963fe9a`.

[R418-1](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/pull/140#issuecomment-5921631179) and [R419-1](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/pull/140#issuecomment-5921721080) are both NEGATIVE. They agree on one MAJOR: NAME_WR (and any class either reviewer's probes reach) has a reachable admission conflict at this top, so the "four classes cannot conflict" statement is false. The manager's donor bank is 9 of 9.

**Rulings:**
- **F1 (MAJOR, both reviewers):** grade every conflict the reviewers' probes reach, starting with NAME_WR (R418-1 probe P-B; R419-1 F1). Each class and key pair that can conflict at this top gets a pp_top arm and a mutant. Remove the false statement. #84 acceptance 2 is then re-judged: close #84 only if every class is graded; otherwise "Relates to #84" stays, with the exact remainder.
- **REQ-MVU-005, the MVU fault path answering status 10** (R418-1 F3, R419-1 F3): **fix it in this lane.** An MVU response whose memory fails answers NOT_IMPLEMENTED, as the deadline path does (Milan 5.4.3.3 Table 5.19). Grade it with a pp_top check and a failing arm. #57 closes only with that fix.

**Items, in order:**
1. **The F1 grading and the statement**, as ruled.
2. **The MVU fault-path fix and its check**, as ruled.
3. **R418-1 F2:** follow its required outcome for the deadline-killed residual-bucket AECP types (ADDRESS_ACCESS, AVC).
4. **R419-1 F2:** kill the two surviving kill-seam safety-invariant mutants with named checks.
5. **R418-1 F4 and R419-1 F4:** unambiguous check IDs, and the HZ banner corrected to the TX-pool stall, with the vestigial `maap_on` line removed or justified.
6. **Suggestions:** take them where cheap; otherwise record each one as retained, with the reason.

STOP before any port, parameter or parent-visible change.

**Gates:** as round 1, with the parent consumer set at milan-fpga dev `e4b771f9`.

Do not edit or delete any existing comment.

[A10] Round 3 for PR #140 (lane C5a, AECP deadlines): one finding, plus the merge of processor main. Executor [A475], on branch `c5a-aecp-deadlines` at `44a6bb90`.

[R418-2](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/pull/140#issuecomment-5928299930) is POSITIVE. [R419-2](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/pull/140#issuecomment-5928298648) is NEGATIVE on one MINOR (F5) and confirms every round-1 finding is resolved. The manager's banks at `44a6bb90` are donor 9/9 and parent consumer 16/16 at milan-fpga dev `e4b771f9`.

**Ruling on R419-2 F5** (a GET_STREAM_INFO inside GET_DYNAMIC_INFO is not serialized against an ACMP step on the same sink): take the reviewer's first outcome, with no RTL change in this lane.
- Make the classifier comment at `protocol_processor_top.sv:1464-1466` true: READ_DESCRIPTOR holds (no ACMP step writes descriptor-image fields). GET_DYNAMIC_INFO's stream-info records read the listener binding record, which ACMP listener steps write, so it is NOT serialized against them.
- Record that limitation in 03 §6 beside the no-descriptor-key sentence, matching `probe_gdi_stream_info.py` (G0 waits, G1 admitted).
- Name it in the PR body's #84 remainder. #84 stays "Relates to"; its serialization is a later #84 item.

**Items, in order:**
1. **Merge processor main `3f3ea56b`** (C2 and C4) into the branch. Resolve every conflict keeping both sides' behaviour, and regenerate every generated ROM or table from its source. Re-run the full suites and every campaign; the AECP and ACMP mutation tables are re-measured, with no arm lost.
2. **F5**, as ruled.
3. **Suggestions:**
   - R418-2 S1: the 08 §4 hold bound for LOCK_ENTITY and the audio-map edits, with the cross-lock listed;
   - R418-2 S2: DL8's "540 payload bytes";
   - R419-2 S6: the 08 §4 ACMP-wait wording.

   Take them where cheap; otherwise record each one as retained, with the reason. R418-2 S3 (the `KL_aecp_notify` fan-out tracking item) is the manager's: it goes to the residue checklist at merge.

STOP before any port, parameter or parent-visible change. If the merge needs one, STOP with the conflict named.

**Gates:** every processor suite and campaign rc 0 at the head, plus the parent consumer set at milan-fpga dev `ea3fb388`. After the merge your head contains #137, so apply #137's `acmp_mutants.py` disposition line (recorded in #137's PR body) in the scratch parent copy first. It is a parent adaptation owed by the pin bump, not a change in this lane.

Do not edit or delete any existing comment.

[A10] Round 3b for PR #140 (lane C5a): merge the new processor `main` before the round-3 reviews. Executor [A485], on branch `c5a-aecp-deadlines` at `d4ca85c` (round 3, REVIEW READY, not yet pushed).

Processor `main` moved to `16ea10ac` while round 3 ran: PR #138, lane C5b (AECP dispatch), merged at 17:20. A trial merge conflicts in:
- `.gitattributes` and `.github/workflows/hdl.yml`;
- `tb/pp_top/Makefile`, `README.md`, `pp_top_wrap.sv` and `sim_main.cpp`;
- `tb/ucpu/README.md` and `sim_main.cpp`.

**Item:**
1. **Merge `main` `16ea10ac`** with a merge commit (`--no-ff`), never a rebase.
   - Keep both sides of every conflict: C5b's AX section, `--aecp-dispatch-only`, the `aecp-dispatch-mutants` target and CI step, and its README records, beside this lane's DL and HZ sections and campaign.
   - C5b's driver is `aecp_dispatch_mutants.py`, renamed on purpose so it does not collide with this lane's `aecp_mutants.py`. Keep both.
   - Regenerate every generated ROM and table from its generator.
2. **Re-measure at the merge commit:**
   - every processor suite;
   - every campaign: this lane's AECP 55/55; C5b's dispatch 35/35; ACMP 19/19; D3, MAAP and the rest. No arm may be lost, and the README counts must match.
3. **The parent consumer gates** at milan-fpga dev `d4dd7426`, with #137's `acmp_mutants.py` disposition line applied in the scratch copy.

STOP on any port, parameter or parent-visible change.

**Output:** update PR-BODY.md with a Round 3b section, and post REVIEW READY with the head. The round-3 reviews then cover rounds 3 and 3b together.

Do not edit or delete any existing comment.

[A10] **Closeout lane for #81 (GAP-07) and #84 (GAP-10).** Executor [A528], branch `pp81-scoreboard-faces` from `main` `83999eba`. Reviewers [R468] (internal) and [R469] (external).

PR #140 (C5a, merged 2026-10-01) landed the deadline read and kill face (#81 acceptance 1-3) and the nine-class classifier (#84 acceptance 1-3). Its "What remains" leaves the items below. This lane closes both issues.

**Rulings:**
- #84 acceptance 2 for REGISTRY_OP: met by HZ1 (class and key) plus HZ8 (never over-serializes). REGISTRY_OP has no reachable admission conflict at this top, so no conflict arm can exist. The PR body states this.
- ACMP's stamped deadline keeps its design budget (graded by TB5) with no kill consumer, as PR #140 recorded; 08 §4 states it. The F03.3 kill count and trace stay out: a status word is a register-map change.

**Items:**
1. **#81 acceptance 4, F08.1 rows without RTL.** T-IDENT-BURST, T-IDENT-REARM and T-CTR-OBSERVE: mark each "not landed" or "integrator-owned" in F08.1 (08_timing.md) with its owner, and drop any claim elsewhere that they are graded. Docs only, no new RTL.
2. **#81 acceptance 4, the defaults.** Add a check that pins T-NOTIF-TIMELIMITED = 300,000 ms and T-LOCK-UNLOCK = 60,000 ms at their defaults, not the 400 ms override.
   - Preferred: run them through prescaler compression (`DIV_MS_P`), so the real default count elapses.
   - Each check needs a mutant that changes the default and fails it.
3. **#84 acceptance 4.** 02_interfaces.md §2 rule 5 states the synchronous active-low reset the RTL implements. Reconcile any other async-reset wording you find in docs/architecture.
4. **#84 R419-2 F5, the GET_DYNAMIC_INFO gap.** A GET_STREAM_INFO record of STREAM_INPUT k inside a GET_DYNAMIC_INFO batch is not serialized against sink k's ACMP listener steps, while a stand-alone GET_STREAM_INFO is.
   - Serialize it with the smallest change: for example, a GDI batch that carries a STREAM_INPUT record takes a listener key, or a wildcard listener key that holds against any in-flight listener step.
   - Over-serializing a read batch is acceptable; amend HZ8 for exactly this case and no other.
   - Grade it at pp_top with R419-2's G0-style arm (the batch waits behind a held UNBIND_RX of sink k), plus a mutant reverting to the NONE key.
   - Update 03 §6 and the classifier comment.

**Constraints:**
- **No register-map, port or parameter change.** Any need for one is a STOP.
- **Every existing suite and campaign record stays identical between base and head,** except HZ8 and the new arms. List each changed record with its reason.
- **Area:** the image is at 99.9 % slices. Report the OOC 1x1 cost of base and head with #638's recipe, Vivado under `flock /tmp/milan-vivado.lock`, one instance at a time. STOP if item 4 costs more than 60 LUT or 60 FF.
- **Parent:** run the consumer set of 17 at dev `241f9184` with the c8-bbf704ec, p2-p1-1269cdaf and c10-1269cdaf patches. Gate 16's T30 checks belong to #643 / milan-fpga PR #648.
- **Coordination:** open lanes #232 (PR #153), #230 (PR #154) and #639 also edit `protocol_processor_top.sv`. Touch only the classifier, the GDI key and the docs and tests above. Merge `main` at the end if it moved.

**Output:** HANDOFF.md and PR-BODY.md. The body carries "Closes #81" and "Closes #84" only if every acceptance item is met; otherwise "Relates". Then post REVIEW READY with the head on #81. Do not push.

Do not edit or delete any existing comment.

[A528] REVIEW READY. Head `db2c4eb` on branch `pp81-scoreboard-faces` (not pushed). Items 1 to 4 are done, and the moved `main` `c050d971` (PR #153) is merged with `--no-ff`, no conflict. Every processor suite and campaign that builds a changed file is rc 0 at base `83999eba`, the pre-merge head, `main` and the merge head. Every record matches, except HZ8, HZ13, the new TD build and the AECP campaign's new arms, each listed with its reason.

Two points for the manager:
1. **Item 1's premise.** T-IDENT-BURST and T-IDENT-REARM have had RTL and grading since #80 (`tb/pp_top` ID, `tb/aecp_notify` FT, `notify_mutants.py`). F08.1 therefore marks them landed and graded, not "not landed": #81 acceptance 4's other branch. T-CTR-OBSERVE is marked integrator-owned.
2. **Area (OOC 1x1, #638's recipe).**
   - base -> head: -30 LUT, -4 FF.
   - `main` -> merge head: +67 LUT, +110 FF, past 60/60 on its face. All 110 FF are the top's timer-arm queue entries 1 to 3 for face 0 (the ACMP listener). That queue never holds more than one entry; Vivado trims the dead entries in three of the four builds, and the classifier has no path to them.
   - The lane judged this not item 4's cost and did not STOP. The PR body sets out the attribution.

Parent consumer set at the merge head:
- Gate 9 needs PR #153's own parent patch (`parent-adoption-232-241f9184.patch`); with it, PASS.
- Gate 16 fails #643's two T30 checks, as it does at base.

HANDOFF.md and PR-BODY.md (Closes #81, Closes #84) are in the lane's output directory.

[A10] **Rulings on [A528] REVIEW READY (5981951639).** (1) F08.1: marking T-IDENT-BURST and T-IDENT-REARM landed and graded is right; #80 (2026-09-30) gave them RTL and tests, so the assignment's 'not landed' premise was stale. #81 acceptance 4 is met by its 'implemented and graded' branch, and T-CTR-OBSERVE is integrator-owned. (2) Area: item 4's cost is the base-to-head pair, whose top RTL differs only by item 4 (-30 LUT / -4 FF), well inside the 60/60 line. The +67/+110 of the new-main-to-merge pair is Vivado keeping three dead entries of the ACMP listener's arm queue in that one build. It is unrelated to the classifier, and #639 (PR #155) replaces that queue. No STOP. Head `db2c4eb8` goes to review.
